title: The attachment's entry topology: what a tether actually bonds to
verificationType: in-silico (C-0020's in-plane membrane lattice, loaded through four entry topologies instead of one, with the orthotropic shear-lag membrane run beside it) + logical (a cut-equilibrium pigeonhole that bounds every topology before a matrix is assembled) + literature (the joint's own allowable as a function of bonded length, from C-0006's own primary source)
acceptance: The peak per-load-path force for the entry topologies an origami attachment actually has, against the one-point-on-one-duplex model, propagated into C-0014's tether geometry and C-0021's preload
maturity: TRL 1-3 — model-consistent and traceable, NOT empirically demonstrated

units.transferRatio: dimensionless, per pN of applied tether force

conventions: x along the helices, y across them; the origin of (x, y) is the centre of the footprint; T-15's conventions, unchanged
an ENTRY TOPOLOGY is a set of bonds, each (duplex, station, share), with the shares summing to one; C-0020's attachment is one bond with share 1
a tether pair's pull direction is the line joining the two ends' CENTROIDS, which keeps the resultants collinear and the load case moment-free
TRANSFER RATIO eta = peak force in one load path / applied tether force; CONCENTRATION FACTOR C = the same peak / the equal share
the PRESCRIBED split gives every bond 1/m of the tension (a compliant staple); the COMPATIBLE split makes all bonds move together (a rigid staple) and is m springs in parallel between two rigid ends
a bond station is an exact multiple of the 0.34 nm rise and is made a node, so the axial force it introduces is resolved rather than averaged
validity: TRL 1-3, model-consistent and traceable; nothing here is measured

everything structural is C-0020's, unchanged — the same sheet, the same crossover stiffness, the same phase machinery, the same allowables — so any difference reported here is the ENTRY TOPOLOGY and nothing else

the compatible split is defined for an ALIGNED pull only: an unequal split at one end of an oblique chord carries a couple that nothing in this model reacts, C-0010's lateral stiffness being exactly zero
the staple's own elasticity is not modelled; the two split limits bracket it

the joint allowable is Strunz et al.'s single-barrier model with THEIR published constants, used inside their measured 16-4000 pN/s and quoted as a RATIO wherever a design decision rests on it; the Evans-Ritchie form has no equilibrium plateau and must not be extrapolated to zero loading rate
the joint allowable is measured on free oligonucleotides pulled at opposite 5' ends, not on a staple domain inside a sheet, and no measurement of the latter exists
no out-of-plane coupling, on C-0020's flat-sheet argument and with its caveat
single layer, static, 300 K, aqueous buffer with Mg2+

provenance.joint allowable: CITED, MEASURED — Strunz, Oroszlan, Schaefer & Guentherodt, PNAS 96:11277 (1999), Eqs. 1-3 with their own fitted alpha = 3 +/- 1, beta = 0.5 +/- 0.1 and a barrier separation of 0.7 A per base pair with a 7 A offset. The 48 +/- 2 pN this programme carries is their 30 bp point at 50 nm/s
provenance.unzip allowable: CITED, MEASURED — Essevaz-Roulet et al., PNAS 94:11935 (1997); length-INDEPENDENT, which is why splitting multiplies it by m
provenance.nicked ceiling: CITED, MEASURED — van Mameren et al., PNAS 106:18231 (2009)
provenance.hold-down scale: C-0021, k_BT / 3.0 nm read as a mean excursion

bounds.name: pigeonhole floor on the transfer ratio
bounds.statement: the duplex axial forces on a cut sum to the applied force (C-0020 gate 3), so on a tile of 15 duplexes SOME duplex carries at least 1/D. No entry topology whatsoever can beat it

bounds.name: ceiling on the duplex-path effective allowable
bounds.statement: the pigeonhole floor turned into an allowable: entry-topology design cannot buy more than D times the single-path allowable, and only a bond to EVERY duplex reaches it, which is an edge clamp and not a tether

bounds.name: short-bond limit for a band of m duplexes
bounds.statement: no crossover sits on the rim, so the entry element of each bonded duplex carries exactly its own share: an m-duplex bond with an equal split enters at 1/m, quoted here for m = 2. C-0020's 'halving' is an upper bound on the benefit, not an estimate

bounds.name: the footprint is the m = 1 case
bounds.statement: spreading a bond over k bases of ONE duplex leaves m = 1, so that duplex must still carry the whole tension inboard of the footprint and the peak cannot fall. Whatever a footprint buys is bought on the JOINT, not on the sheet

bounds.name: the joint allowable is concave above its break-even
bounds.statement: Strunz's own scaling makes the shear rupture force saturate with domain length, so m domains of n/m outperform one of n above this total bonded length in base pairs — and UNDERperform it below, because the barrier separation has an n-independent offset

verdict.the headline survives, and it was never: C-0020's eta = 1.0000 is reproduced exactly by the general load introduction (1.0000), and every entry topology obeys the pigeonhole floor 1/D = 0.0667. But the sheet has almost nothing to say about the entry topology: a bond spanning m duplexes enters at exactly 1/m and the peak exceeds that by at most 4.69 %, so the ladder is arithmetic, not mechanics. What the entry topology really decides is the allowable of the JOINT, and that is a sequence-design choice with a measured law behind it.
verdict.the halving is exact to a per cent, and: A two-duplex bond with an equal split gives eta = 0.5000 against the exact 1/2 at the best of the 448 (pair, phase) designs and 0.5202 at the worst — a 4.0 % spread over every pair and every column phase. A RIGID staple splits 0.5569 / 0.4431 instead of 50/50 at worst (duplexes 0 and 1, phase 6 bp), which is x1.0705 on the peak. So the two split limits — a compliant staple and a rigid one — bracket the answer to under 11.4 %, and the halving needs no model of the staple's own elasticity, which is the one thing nothing in the literature supplies.
verdict.what it costs in the crossover path: not: It PAYS. Both bonded duplexes move together, so the interface between them slides less rather than more: the peak crossover force falls from 0.1826 to 0.0969 per pN of tension going from one duplex to two. Over the whole ladder of 3840 designs the crossover path never becomes the binding one — its closest approach is x1.07 the duplex-limited tension, and it recedes as the band widens, because splitting the load across duplexes relieves the interfaces FASTER than it relieves the duplexes. The binding path is the duplex axial force at every one of them.
verdict.bonding onto a crossover buys nothing th: A tether bonded onto a crossover is a two-duplex bond that is forced to sit at an interior station, and the control that isolates the two — one point on one duplex at the SAME station — shows the topology worth x1.568 to x1.814 in the effective allowable over 448 designs, against the x2.00 the two-duplex bond is worth at the rim. The crossover adds nothing mechanically: what it costs is the chord, 21.8 nm instead of 40, because the columns sit strictly inside the footprint.
verdict.the footprint is not a sheet variable: n: Spreading the bond over a footprint leaves m = 1, so the duplex must still carry the whole tension inboard of it. At the nominal phase the peak does fall, from 1.0000 at 1 bp to 0.8622 at 20 bp — but the SAME single-point attachment read at the inboard end of the same footprint carries 0.7195, so that relief is the load SHED past the first crossover column and not a property of the entry topology at all. The column phase decides where that column falls, and over the complete 32-phase sweep the worst case is eta = 1.0000 at 8 bp and 0.9143 at 20 bp: at the phases that put the first column further from the rim than the footprint is long, the whole bond enters before anything can shed and the footprint buys NOTHING. A footprint is not a sheet variable. What it moves is the JOINT: 8 to 20 bp takes the shear allowable from 18.8 to 39.5 pN, x2.10, and THAT is the whole of what it buys.
verdict.splitting a bond has a break-even length: On the JOINT side the two effects run against each other: splitting a bond of n base pairs into m domains of n/m divides the load by m but also shortens each domain. Strunz's own scaling — the barrier separation linear in n with a 7 A offset, ln(off-rate) linear in n — makes the rupture force concave and saturating at 68.1 pN, so splitting WINS above a total bonded length of 14.3 bp and LOSES below it. At the reference 100 pN/s a 32 bp staple split into two 16 bp domains gains x1.445 on the joint AND x2.00 on the sheet; an 8 bp staple split into two 4 bp domains loses x2.582 on the joint and cannot be recovered by any sheet effect.
verdict.the 48 pN is a 30 bp number, and that is: C-0020, C-0014 and C-0009 all consume 48 pN as the per-path shear allowable. It is Strunz's measurement on a 30 bp duplex, and the entry topology is exactly what fixes the length: a realistic 16 bp staple extension gives 34.8 pN and an 8 bp one 18.8 pN. So the one-point model is not conservative about the attachment — it is optimistic by x1.35 unless the tether's joint is 30 bp long, which nothing in the programme has ever said it is. This is CH-0029.
verdict.layout is still worth exactly nothing, a: Over the complete 32 base-pair phase sweep the binding duplex-axial path moves by x1.0000 at a band width of one and x1.0041 at two — the prescribed split makes the entered share a matter of arithmetic, and no arrangement of crossovers can touch it. The RIGID split does depend on the layout, because the compliance matrix does, and it is worth x1.1137 in the largest share: below C-0015's x1.43-1.60 out of plane, and well below the topology's own x2.00. C-0020's 'exactly nothing' is exact at a band width of one and holds to a per cent everywhere else.
verdict.the oblique overshoot is relieved, but n: C-0020's worst aligned-family overshoot — an oblique chord whose moment the crossovers react as an axial couple — reaches eta = 2.3290 at a single point and 2.0039 through a two-duplex bond, a relief of x1.16 against the x2.00 the same bond buys when aligned. The couple is applied by the chord's transverse component and a band at one station barely changes its arm; what the band does is divide the axial share, and only that part of the overshoot follows.
verdict.which way the net design moves: A topology that raises the effective allowable shortens the minimum tether and RAISES the preload at that minimum, because F_z = n A sqrt(2A/S) goes as A^1.5. The 32 bp staple split across two duplexes takes A_eff from 48.0 to 69.6 pN, L_min at the desired 10 nm stroke from 33.5 to 27.7 nm, and the four-tether preload from 54.9 to 94.6 pN — i.e. from 55 % to 95 % of the §3 100 pN target. C-0021 wants a downward preload but only 1.38 pN of it, so everything above that is a tax on the actuator, and the design should sit at whatever tether length delivers the wanted preload rather than at L_min: 116.6 nm at the 10 nm stroke. The entry topology's value is that it makes MORE of that length axis admissible, not that the shortest tether is the one to build.
verdict.maturity: TRL 1-3. Model-consistent and traceable. NOT empirically demonstrated. No in-plane force in a loaded origami sheet has ever been measured; the crossover's in-plane stiffness is not in the literature in any form; and the joint allowable is an Evans-Ritchie extrapolation of a 1999 AFM measurement on free oligonucleotides, not on a staple in a sheet.
